sentences.text: That the major aspect / ground on which the impugned complaint is liable to be set aside / quashed against the petitioner is that the respondent has not arrayed the Company (M/s Zee Laboratories Ltd) as an accused in the impugned complaint.

It is submitted that on the plain reading section 34 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940,
"if a person who commits an offence under the Act is a company, the company as well as every person in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of business of the company at time of commission of offence is deemed to be guilty of the offence".

It is worthwhile to mention here that the Explanation to the said Section further explains that for the purposes of this Section "Company" means a body corporate and includes of "company" or other association of individuals.
Further "Director" in relation to a company means a Partner in the firm.

Hence, it is emphasized that section 34 of the Act is concerned with the offences by the company or a firm and it makes the other persons vicariously liable for commission of an offence on the part of the company and such vicarious liability only gets attracted when the condition precedent laid down under the section 34 stands satisfied and such condition undoubtedly is arraigning of company / firm as an accused in the impugned complaint.

There is well settled law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Aneeta Hada V/s Godfather Travels & Tours Ltd. 2012 (5) SCC 661 that commission of an offence by the company / firm is an express condition precedent to attract the vicarious liability of other persons / directors and the words "as well as the company" appearing in the section 34 make it absolutely and unmistakably clear that when the company / firm is prosecuted, then only the persons mentioned in other categories could be vicariously liable for the offence subject to the averments in the petition and prove thereof, thus, for maintaining the prosecution under section 34 of the Act against partners, arraigning of a company /
firm as an accused is imperative.

According to Mr. Varut Gupta appearing counsel for the petitioner, the impugned complaint was not liable to be entertained by the trial Court, in that, the complainant respondent herein did not array the Manufacturing Company, namely, M/s Zee Laboratories Ltd as an accused therein the complaints and instead impleaded the petitioner herein alone being its authorized signatory, in breach and violation of the mandate of Section 34 of the Act of 1940 and that both the courts below over looked the mandate of the said Section 34 of the Act of 1940 and in the process, grossly erred or in law.

According to Mr. Gupta, Section 34 of Act of 1940 is pari materia with Section 141 of Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881 and the Apex Court while interpreting the provisions of Section of 141 of the said Act has ruled that for maintaining a prosecution under the said Act of 1881 against a company for an offence committed by such company, arraying of the company as an accused is imperative and that the other offenders connected with such company can only be implicated on the touch stone of vicarious liability.

Mr. Gupta in support of his aforesaid submissions would heavily rely upon the judgments of the Apex Court passed in case titled as Aneeta Hada vs. Godfather Travel and Tours Private ltd.
C/w reported in (2012) 5 SCC 661 and Dilip Hariramani vs. Bank of Baroda, reported in AIR 2022 (SC) 2258.

Sub-section (1) to Section 141 of the NI Act states that where a company commits an offence, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of and was responsible to C/w the company for the conduct of the business, as well as the company itself, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence.
The expression every person is wide and comprehensive enough to include a director, partner or other officers or persons.

At the same time, it follows that a person who does not bear out the requirements of in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business is not vicariously liable under Section 141 of the NI Act.
The burden is on the prosecution to show that the person prosecuted was in charge of and responsible to the company for conduct of its business.

The proviso, which is in the nature of an exception, states that a person liable under subsection (1) shall not be punished if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he had exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.
The onus to satisfy the requirements and take benefit of the proviso is on the accused.
Still, it does not displace or extricate the initial onus and burden on the prosecution to first establish the requirements of sub-section (1) to Section 141 of the NI Act.

The proviso gives immunity to a person who is otherwise vicariously liable under sub-section (1) to Section 141 of the NI Act."

5.
The petitioner herein claims to be the authorized signatory of Drug Manufacturing Company namely, M/s Zee Laboratories ltd. having its registered office at 913, D-Mall Neta ji Subash Place,
Pitampura, Delhi possessed of a licence under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 for manufacturing, sale and distribution of the drugs.
6.
The respondent 1 herein is stated to have filed a criminal complaint against the petitioner herein before the trial court alleging therein the commission of offence under Section 18(a)(i) read with Section 27 of the Drug and Cosmetic Act, 1940, impleading proforma respondents 2 and 3 therein in the said complaint as accused 1 and 2 and the petitioner herein as accused 3 while complaining that a drug namely, "Aceflex-P Suspension" upon analysis by the Government Analyst, was found to be not of standard quality.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
That throughout the length and breadth of the petition of complaint there is no reference to the actual role played by the petitioner in the alleged offence which is the subject matter of the instant case and in the absence of any such specific role being attributed to the petitioner, no criminal proceedings can be initiated against the petitioner.

2 ii.
There is well settled law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Aneeta Hada V/s Godfather Travels & Tours Ltd. 2012 (5) SCC 661 that commission of an offence by the company / firm is an express condition precedent to attract the vicarious liability of other persons / directors and the words "as well as the company" appearing in the section 34 make it absolutely and unmistakably clear that when the company / firm is prosecuted, then only the persons mentioned in other categories could be vicariously liable for the offence subject to the averments in the petition and prove thereof, thus, for maintaining the prosecution under section 34 of the Act against partners, arraigning of a company /
firm as an accused is imperative.
That the proceedings by virtue of impugned complaint against the petitioner is further bad on the ground that the respondent / complainant has failed to establish extent of liability against the petitioner in terms of Section 34 of the Act.
There is well settled law that unless and until the prosecution / complainant arrayed the company / firm as an accused, the prosecution against the Director /
Partner does not hold good in the eyes of law.
Before proceeding to advert to the aforesaid submissions of Mr. Gupta, it would be appropriate to refer to Section 34 of the Act, 1940 as also Section 141 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881, which are reproduced as such here under:
34. Offences by companies.--(1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company, every person who at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly:
Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.

7 (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary or other officer of the company, such director, manager, secretary or other officer shall also be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
Thus, the words "as well as the company" appearing in the Section make it absolutely unmistakably clear that when the company can be prosecuted, then only the persons mentioned in the other categories could be vicariously liable for the offence subject to the averments in the petition and proof thereof.
One cannot be oblivious of the fact that the company is a juristic person and it has its own respectability.
If a finding is recorded against it, it would create a concavity in its reputation.
There can be situations when the corporate reputation is affected when a director is indicted.
59 In view of our aforesaid analysis, we arrive at the irresistible conclusion that for maintaining the prosecution under Section 141 of the Act, arraigning of a company as an accused is imperative.
The other categories of offenders can only be brought in the dragnet on the touchstone of vicarious liability as the same has been stipulated in the provision itself.

Still, it does not displace or extricate the initial onus and burden on the prosecution to first establish the requirements of sub-section (1) to Section 141 of the NI Act.

The proviso gives immunity to a person who is otherwise vicariously liable under sub-section (1) to Section 141 of the NI Act."
